Tantamount

/TAN-tuh-mownt/ - rhymes with amount · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Tantamount means equivalent in effect to something graver.

In the old harbor code, dimming your lamp at night was tantamount to piracy.

Worked Example

On a rope team, the mountaineering manual is blunt. Unclipping from the line without calling it out, whatever the reason, is treated as abandoning your partners — not similar to abandoning them, not a lesser cousin of it. Guides who unclip silently lose their certification under the same clause as guides who walk away.

Tantamount is the exact word for that clause, because tantamount means equivalent in effect or meaning — the quiet unclip amounts to abandonment even though nobody walked anywhere. Notice the word's fixed frame: one thing is tantamount to another, and almost always to something grave. Similar compares; tantamount convicts.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

equal: the plain word for matching in measure or effect

as good as: the everyday idiom for the same verdict — as good as stealing

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

unlike: not comparable at all

worlds apart: so different no scale holds them both

Where it sits · whether the likeness carries a verdict — akin → equivalent → tantamount

akin vs. tantamount: Akin claims only kinship — the two things resemble each other, and there the claim ends.

equivalent vs. tantamount: Equivalent stops short of tantamount — equivalents match in measure or effect, neutrally; tantamount passes a verdict, declaring that the act amounts to the graver thing itself.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — tant

Root — tant: so much (Latin tantum)

Root — amount

Root — amount: to add up to (Old French amonter, to go up — Latin ad montem, to the mountain)

Put it together

Put it together: Tant (so much) + amount (add up to) = amounting to just so much. Anglo-French tant amunter meant to add up to as much; English fused the phrase into one adjective for acts that climb, like a column of figures, to the very same height as something graver.

Use the root in a new word: surmount

Use the root in a new word: surmount: Sur- means over, so a team that surmounts an obstacle climbs up and over it — the same mont-, the mountain, hiding in amount and tantamount alike.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / judicial

Tantamount lives in one groove: X is tantamount to Y, where Y is graver than X and the sentence is a verdict — silence tantamount to consent, a walkout tantamount to a forfeit. Equivalent is its neutral cousin for recipes and math; equal is plainer still. If nothing is being weighed in effect, reach for the neutral word.
